case_grain: province x municipality x item x harmonized_nsu_unit x corrected_unit
item: ice cream, sorbet, edible ice (eg., ice-lolli, halo-halo)
notes: The rescue rule in nsu_restate_weights.do decides 'does this case keep a preloaded rung' at the grain province x municipality x item x harmonized_nsu_unit -- WITHOUT corrected_unit. Ice cream is a mixed-dimension item (docs/data_oddities.md sec.4), so this case splits into a g case and an mL case downstream. The g-side had a preloaded row and survived; the mL-side's only price-quantity row was vendor-priced (actual_price=12) and got dropped because the rule saw the g-side's preloaded row as 'this case keeps a preloaded rung' and pooled across both corrected_unit splits. At the grain the pipeline actually pools on, the mL case had nothing to fall back on and lost its only price-quantity observation. Not corrected here per the no-.do-edits rule; fix is to add corrected_unit to the rescue rule's grouping variables.

description: THE ANSWER: why '315 -> 310, five unaccounted' is not a real gap
notes: 315 is a COARSE-grain input count (no corrected_unit; includes the carrot cell). 310 is the FINE-grain output count (with corrected_unit; the grain the pipeline actually uses, and the one this brief specifies). Differencing them subtracts two counts of two different case populations. Measured consistently: coarse loses 12 (315->303), fine loses 14 (324->310 / 323->310 after the Stage-2 loss). The 14 fine-grain losses are ALL individually named above: 11 unique_mun_price-only + 1 carrot + 1 restate-stage grain-mismatch casualty (ice cream mL) + 1 no-usable-w_ref casualty (CAPIZ/TAPAZ chicken). The apparent 'five missing' is an artifact of comparing across grains, not five additional unexplained cases.
